tagline: Pecan groves and working fields connect four Georgia byway towns
intro: The Enduring Farmlands Scenic Byway links Hawkinsville, Rochelle, Abbeville and Pineview through fields, pecan groves and horse and cattle pastures. Between the towns, two-lane roads run beside agricultural land in Pulaski and Wilcox counties. Georgia DOT includes it among the state’s designated scenic byways, highlighting the area’s continuing agricultural heritage and rural character. Along Highways 129 and 233, fields of corn, cotton, peanuts and soybeans share the roadside with pastures and pecan groves. Farm buildings, churches and houses punctuate the rural stretches; the towns bring the route through older commercial and residential districts.

The campaign for a two-county byway began in 2001, then paused. Hawkinsville, Pulaski County and Hawkinsville Better Hometown revived it in 2008. An initial route linked Hawkinsville, Rochelle and Pineview; participants then proposed adding Abbeville and Cannonville Road. The expanded application won Georgia DOT approval in July 2009, before the corridor management plan was prepared.

Begin at Hawkinsville’s Opera House and head south on Highway 129 past Mile Branch Park and the harness track. Highways 233 and 112 lead to Rochelle; U.S. 280 continues east to Abbeville. Cannonville Road and Highway 112 lead back toward Pineview, with Richland Church Road and Highway 129 completing the return to Hawkinsville.

moments.title: Hawkinsville Opera House
moments.text: The City Auditorium combined a stage with city government: the building originally housed both City Hall and a 576-seat auditorium. Designed by W.R. Gunn, the Opera House had the county’s largest public seating capacity. It accommodated church services after a church fire and films after the local movie theater burned in the early 1950s. A rehabilitation between 1999 and 2001 restored and augmented its original lighting system and added a copper roof. The work also installed upholstered seats in a historical style, updated plumbing and mechanical systems, and added an elevator and restrooms.

moments.title: Hawkinsville harness track
moments.text: The Lawrence Bennett harness track lies south of Mile Branch Park along Highway 129. Hawkinsville has hosted harness racing events since 1894. Beginning in the 1920s, horses from colder climates came here to train through the mild winters. In 2010, the facility housed and trained Standardbred horses from October through April. The city celebrates its connection to the sport with an annual Harness Horse Festival.

moments.title: Abbeville
moments.text: Abbeville’s courthouse marks a county seat established when Wilcox County was formed in 1857. The first county courthouse was built in 1858; the present building belongs to the early twentieth century. The present courthouse is a Neoclassical Revival design by Frank P. Milburn. Its site also helps locate an episode from the Confederacy’s collapse. Jefferson Davis camped just north of the present courthouse site on May 8, 1865; Union troops captured him two days later at Irwinville. The byway reaches Abbeville along U.S. 280, then turns toward Cannonville Road for the journey back to Pineview.
